description: Iterate the dashboard to be more fluid and visually nicer (inspired by _ref-athen Dashboard.tsx), convert the lesson-open flow from a route navigation into a POP-UP modal overlaying the dashboard, and make the trail auto-update on lesson completion via react-query invalidation. This is the core frontend feature. Build ON the existing dashboard (do NOT rip it out). All completion/locking state stays server-authoritative via useCourseTrail; do NOT copy the reference repo's temporary local-only completion toggle.
steps: FLUIDITY/VISUALS (DashboardPage.tsx + src/styles/theme.css): iterate the existing trail to be smoother and nicer, keeping the existing structure (square module nodes, circle lesson nodes, carousel, Cursos/Salas selector, top-down panel). Inspired by _ref-athen/codigo-base/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx (reference only): (a) a per-module gradient background on the trail layer that transitions smoothly when the focused/current module changes (drive it from currentColor / the focused module color already computed in DashboardPage via resolveModuleColor; animate with a CSS transition on background/background-image using CSS custom properties like --trail-color, do NOT introduce Tailwind); (b) a smoother connector between nodes - replace or augment the current ::before line segments with an SVG smooth path (or improved CSS) whose segment colors follow the per-module colors, falling back to --brand-purple; (c) smoother centering of the focused node (the existing computeCenterScrollLeft + container.scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'}) is the base - keep it; refine easing/offsets if helpful). Keep it responsive (CSS vars, existing @media rules).

Extract pure helpers for any new trail geometry/segment-coloring/gradient math into src/features/dashboard/helpers.ts (e.g. a function that maps module colors to gradient stops, or computes SVG path segment coordinates/colors) so they are unit-testable without the DOM. Keep existing exported helpers and their behavior intact.

LESSON POP-UP: change the dashboard's lesson-open behavior so that clicking an available (not locked) lesson node opens a POP-UP modal overlaying the dashboard instead of navigating to /lesson/:id. In DashboardPage.tsx, replace onOpenLesson={(id) => navigate(`/lesson/${id}`)} with opening a modal that renders the lesson runner for that lesson id. Reuse the shared Modal primitive (src/components/ui/Modal.tsx) or the app's modal approach (CourseDetailModal pattern) - do not build a new overlay from scratch.

Extract the lesson-doing UI from src/features/lesson/LessonView.tsx into a reusable component (e.g. LessonRunner) that takes a lessonId prop (and optional roomId + onCompleted callback) and contains the question-rendering + finalize flow currently in LessonView. LessonView (the /lesson/:id route) should then render LessonRunner using the :id param so the standalone route keeps working. The dashboard renders LessonRunner inside the Modal. Preserve all existing lesson behavior (4 question types, server-authoritative finalize_attempt via useFinalizeLesson, results display, 'Refazer aula'). Do NOT add new lint warnings (LessonView.tsx already has one pre-existing warning at line 70 about the 'questions' useMemo dependency - keep it as-is or fix it, but do not add more).

AUTO TRAIL UPDATE: when a lesson is finalized successfully, the dashboard trail must visually update automatically (completed node + next unlocked) with no manual reload. Wire react-query invalidation on finalize success: in src/features/lesson/api.ts useFinalizeLesson, add an onSuccess that calls queryClient.invalidateQueries for the dashboard trail and overview queries (dashboardKeys.trail / dashboardKeys.overview from src/features/dashboard/api.ts) and the lesson progress key (lessonKeys.progress). Prefer invalidating by the stable prefix (e.g. ['dashboard']) so both the active course trail and overview refetch. Since finalize_attempt is server-authoritative, drive the visual update purely from refetched completion state - do NOT introduce any local fake-completion toggle. When the lesson pop-up reports completion (onCompleted or the mutation settling), the modal can stay open to show results (as LessonView does today) while the underlying trail refetches; closing the modal returns to an already-updated trail. Ensure the useFinalizeLesson hook has access to a QueryClient (useQueryClient) - it currently does not import useQueryClient, so add it.
Keep the /lesson/:id route in src/App.tsx working (it may still be used by deep links / rooms). The PRIMARY flow from the dashboard becomes the pop-up.
Extend src/features/dashboard/__tests__/helpers.test.ts with tests for any new pure helpers added in step 2 (gradient stop mapping, segment colors, geometry). Do not weaken existing tests.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard trail is visibly more fluid: the trail background is a per-module gradient that transitions smoothly when the focused module changes, and node-to-node connectors are smoother (SVG path or improved segments) with per-module colors, all using CSS custom properties (no Tailwind).

Clicking an available lesson node on the dashboard opens a modal pop-up over the dashboard content (NO navigation to /lesson/:id) that renders the full lesson runner (content + 4 question types + Finalizar + results).
The lesson runner UI is a reusable component used BOTH inside the dashboard modal AND by the /lesson/:id route (LessonView), with no behavior regression.

After finalizing a lesson from the pop-up, the dashboard trail updates automatically (just-completed node shows completed, the next lesson unlocks) without a manual page reload, driven by react-query invalidation of the dashboard trail/overview queries - no local fake-completion state.
npm run build passes; npm run typecheck passes; npm run lint has no NEW warnings beyond the 6 pre-existing; npm run test passes including new helper tests.
The /lesson/:id route still renders the lesson runner correctly.
verification: Run 'npm run build' (authoritative) and confirm it is green.
Run 'npm run typecheck', 'npm run lint' (no new warnings), 'npm run test' (all pass, new dashboard helper tests included).

Code review: confirm onOpenLesson opens a Modal rendering the reusable lesson component rather than calling navigate('/lesson/...'); confirm useFinalizeLesson onSuccess invalidates dashboardKeys.trail/overview and lessonKeys.progress; confirm no local completion toggle was introduced and completion remains derived from useCourseTrail/completions.
